images.title: Rule of Three: the mid-day meal
images.purpose: Shows 120 students needing 15 kg of rice and 80 students needing 10 kg, with one factor 2/3 applied to both.
images.composition: Two boxes side by side with one wide arrow between them. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: Left box, outlined in teal (#0072B2): top line '120 students', bottom line '15 kg rice'. Right box, outlined in amber (#E69F00): top line '80 students', bottom line '10 kg rice', with '10 kg rice' in reddish purple (#CC79A7). One wide dark outline colour (#2B2B2B) arrow from the left box to the right box, labelled '× 2/3'. Exactly 2 boxes, 1 arrow, no food drawings.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Three quantities are known; multiply the fourth by the same factor of change.
images.description: Shows 120 students needing 15 kg of rice and 80 students needing 10 kg, with one factor 2/3 applied to both.

image_decisions.why: The single factor applied to both rows is the Rule of Three, and two boxes make the three knowns and one unknown clear.
